 1          Pursuant to Civil Local Rule 16-9, the Standing Order for All Judges of the Northern District of
 2   California – Contents of Joint Case Management Statement, and Standing Order for Civil Cases Before
 3   Judge Eumi K. Lee, Plaintiff Apple Inc. (“Apple”), Defendant Chen Shi, Defendant Guangdong Oppo
 4   Mobile Telecommunications Corp., Ltd., Defendant InnoPeak Technology, Inc., and Defendant Zijing
 5   Zeng (collectively, “the Parties”) respectfully submit this Joint Case Management Statement. The Parties
 6   certify that their respective lead trial counsel have met and conferred for the preparation of this statement
 7   as required by Civil Local Rule 16-3:
 8   I.     JURISDICTION AND SERVICE
 9          The Parties agree that jurisdiction and venue are proper. This Court has original jurisdiction over
10   this action pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1331 and supplemental jurisdiction pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1367(a).
11   Venue is proper pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b). Defendants do not contest service.
12   II.    FACTS
13          A.      Apple’s Statement
14          Apple is a global technology company recognized for its innovative consumer electronics
15   products. Since its founding in 1976, Apple has introduced transformative products like the Macintosh,
16   iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and AirPods. Dkt. 251 ¶ 48. Apple’s release of its first-generation Apple
17   Watch in 2015 set a new standard for smartwatches, distinguishing itself not only with its robust health
18   and fitness tracking features but also with its sleek, customizable design and its seamless integration across
19   the Apple ecosystem. Id. ¶ 79. Apple’s innovative health sensing technology is a key area of its cutting-
20   edge technologies and product design. Id. Health sensing technology uses small sensors to collect,
21   process, and transmit data related to the wearer’s physiological signals, movements, and environment.
22   This allows monitoring of metrics such as heart rate, temperature, blood oxygen, sleep patterns, and
23   more—creating actionable insights into health, fitness, and well-being. Id.
24          Apple has spent billions of dollars researching new technologies and developing a wide range of
25   consumer electronic products. Id. ¶ 52. Apple’s substantial investments in research and other forms of
26   innovation deserve protection, and Apple relies on its trade secrets, in addition to its copyrights, patents,
27   and trademarks, to guard the ingenuity and industry of its employees. Id.
28

 1          Defendant Chen Shi (“Dr. Shi”) worked at Apple from September 2019 through his termination in
 2   late-June 2025. During his employment at Apple, Dr. Shi was entrusted with valuable trade secret
 3   information about Apple Watch, including its design and development documentation, internal
 4   specifications, and product roadmaps. Id. ¶ 5. Dr. Shi knew well the importance of maintaining the
 5   confidentiality of this information.    Upon joining Apple, Dr. Shi executed a Confidentiality and
 6   Intellectual Property Agreement (“IPA”), (id. ¶ 6), and received numerous trainings throughout his tenure
 7   at Apple. Despite his legal obligations, and his ethical obligations to his fellow engineers to maintain the
 8   secrecy of their work product, Dr. Shi conspired to steal Apple’s trade secrets relating to Apple Watch
 9   and to disclose them to Dr. Zeng and his new employers, OPPO and InnoPeak. Id. ¶ 7.
10          After salary discussion with OPPO, but before leaving Apple, Dr. Shi told Dr. Zeng that he planned
11   to “collect as much information as possible” from Apple while still at Apple and to “share [Apple’s
12   information] with you all later” after starting his new job with OPPO and InnoPeak. OPPO and
13   InnoPeak—through Dr. Zeng and others—expressly informed, encouraged, and approved Dr. Shi’s plan.
14   Id. ¶ 1. Dr. Shi then executed the plan. In the weeks leading up to his departure, he gathered highly
15   sensitive information about Apple Watch, including by downloading highly sensitive documents from an
16   internal Apple system and transferring those files to a USB one day before his departure. Id. ¶¶ 9, 10.
17   Concealing his impending employment with a direct competitor, Dr. Shi also set up and attended dozens
18   of one-on-one meetings with Apple Watch technical team members to learn about their ongoing research
19   and development efforts, including their work on optical sensors, temperature sensors, and ECG sensors.
20   Id.
21          Apple filed its complaint on August 21, 2025, asserting trade secrets misappropriation claims
22   against InnoPeak and OPPO and a breach of contract claim against Dr. Shi. On August 22, 2025, Apple
23   filed a motion for a TRO, Order to Show Cause, and requested expedited discovery (“Apple’s TRO
24   Application”). Shortly thereafter, to resolve Apple’s TRO without Court intervention, OPPO, InnoPeak,
25   and Dr. Shi entered into a stipulation with Apple, which the Court granted, to refrain from accessing or
26   using Apple confidential information, to preserve documents, and to immediately provide the Apple
27   documents they retained for forensic inspection. Dkt. 30. Dr. Shi and Dr. Zeng were placed on leave. Id.

 1           Expedited discovery confirmed that, in the first six weeks of Dr. Shi’s employment with OPPO
 2   and InnoPeak, Defendants disseminated Apple’s trade secrets, including via Dr. Shi’s presentation of
 3   Apple’s trade secrets to hundreds of OPPO and InnoPeak engineers. Id. ¶ 2. Certain slides from Dr. Shi’s
 4   presentation contain images copied directly from the Apple trade secret materials that were
 5   misappropriated. OPPO, InnoPeak, and Dr. Zeng not only encouraged these disclosures; they touted them,
 6   advertising Dr. Shi’s presentation to their personnel as one at which they would learn about “how Apple’s
 7   sensors are developed” from a “former Apple technical director” (even though Dr. Shi was not a director
 8   at Apple). Id. ¶ 13.
 9           On November 3, 2025, Apple amended its complaint under Rule 15(a)(1)(B), and again pursuant
10   to Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a)(2) on January 5, 2026, adding Dr. Zeng as an additional defendant. On January
11   30, 2026, Defendants filed motions to dismiss Apple’s SAC and briefing was completed on February 20,
12   2026.
13           On November 14, 2025, Apple filed a motion seeking a preliminary injunction, and the Court held
14   a hearing on March 10, 2026. The Parties submitted a Joint Status Report pursuant to the Court’s order
15   related to the scope of relief in Apple’s preliminary injunction motion on March 28, 2026. Dkt. 382.
16           B.     Defendants’ Statements
17           Defendants deny that they have misappropriated any Apple trade secret and deny that they
18   encouraged or participated in any such misappropriation. Defendants further deny that Apple has
19   identified any protectable trade secret with the particularity the law requires. Apple’s narrative rests on
20   inference and characterization rather than evidence, and the record developed during expedited and
21   preliminary injunction discovery refutes that narrative at every step.
22                  1.      OPPO’s Statement
23           OPPO is a global technology company with its own substantial health-sensing research.
24   Guangdong OPPO Mobile Telecommunications Corp., Ltd. (“OPPO”) was founded in 2004, employs
25   over 40,000 people across more than 60 countries, and has ranked among the top five global smartphone
26   vendors for years. Guan Decl. (Dkt. 333-35) ¶ 2; Efimov Decl. (Dkt. 333-49) ¶ 33. The company invests
27   substantially in its own research and development, having filed over 110,000 patent applications. Id.
28   OPPO independently developed its own wrist temperature sensing technology beginning no later than

 1   2020 and 2021, years before Dr. Shi was associated with OPPO or InnoPeak. Peng Decl. (Dkt. 335-31)
 2   ¶¶ 41–81, 123–126; Young Decl. (Dkt. 335-35) §§ V.B, IX. OPPO’s thermal models are complex, multi-
 3   dimensional models tailored to OPPO’s own product architecture and materials. Peng Decl. (Dkt. 335-31)
 4   ¶¶ 100–101.
 5          InnoPeak hired Dr. Shi as a Technical Director effective June 30, 2025, and he was employed for
 6   approximately seven weeks before Apple filed suit. Yin Decl. (Dkt. 333-39) ¶18; Preliminary Injunction
 7   Opp. (Dkt. 332-40) at 6. During that period, he had limited interactions with OPPO and its engineering
 8   teams, and focused primarily on learning about OPPO’s existing research-and-development efforts. Dr.
 9   Shi did not transmit any Apple documents to OPPO or any other defendant. And while Dr. Shi provided
10   some generalized suggestions to OPPO, none of his suggestions were incorporated into any OPPO
11   product. Peng Decl. (Dkt. 335-31) ¶¶ 86–89, 99-102.
12          The contemporaneous record confirms the opposite of Apple’s theory. OPPO maintains and
13   enforces robust policies prohibiting the receipt or use of third-party confidential information and trade
14   secrets, requires interviewer training and new-hire commitments, and had Dr. Shi complete trade secret
15   protection training on July 9, 2025. Guan Decl. (Dkt. 333-35) ¶¶ 4–12. When OPPO learned of Apple’s
16   allegations, OPPO and InnoPeak acted immediately to preserve the status quo by revoking Dr. Shi’s
17   system access, suspending his physical access, and issuing a litigation preservation notice. Guan Decl.
18   (Dkt. 333-35) ¶¶ 13–18; Peng Decl. (Dkt. 335-31) ¶ 129. Out of an abundance of caution, OPPO also
19   placed Dr. Zeng on administrative leave. OPPO also entered into the stipulation that the Court granted on
20   August 26, 2025 (Dkt. 30), without admitting to Apple’s allegations or the merits of any requested relief
21   and has complied with it since. Through expedited discovery, OPPO identified more than 400 information-
22   technology repositories, collected and searched the relevant systems and custodial data for Dr. Shi, Dr.
23   Zeng, and 25 additional custodians, ran the search terms Apple itself proposed, and forensically analyzed
24   the devices in its possession. That search did not reveal any protectable Apple trade secret, confidential,
25   or proprietary information in OPPO's possession, custody, or control. Guan Decl. (Dkt. 333-35) ¶¶ 17–27.
26          That exhaustive search confirms what the nature of the alleged trade secrets independently
27   establishes: all of Apple's alleged trade secrets rest on publicly available information. Because Dr. Shi did
28   not transmit any Apple documents to the other defendants, Apple asserts that Dr. Shi created internal

 1   presentations discussing thermal-sensing information, the use of PPG sensors, and various engineering
 2   methodologies, which purportedly reflect Apple trade secrets. But these alleged trade secrets comprise
 3   nothing more than publicly available information. The thermal-sensing concepts were publicly disclosed
 4   before Dr. Shi’s presentations, much of it in Apple’s own published patents and applications and in
 5   fundamental physics. Young Decl. (Dkt. 335-35) §§ V.A, VIII. The PPG-in-earbud concepts were
 6   likewise public, and OPPO independently studied them through a teardown of commercially available
 7   competitor products three months before Dr. Shi joined. Efimov Decl. (Dkt. 333-49) ¶¶ 31, 149–174; Peng
 8   Decl. (Dkt. 335-31) ¶¶ 78–81. And the engineering methodologies that Apple claims are confidential are
 9   instead derived from generally recognized, decades-old industry frameworks. Haughey Decl. (Dkt. 335-
10   33) ¶¶ 14–19.
11          The two OPPO presentations that Apple identifies in its allegations did not disclose any Apple
12   trade secret information. Dr. Shi’s July 16, 2025 wrist temperature presentation contained five slides of
13   publicly known formulas and stock images sourced from public websites, delivered to two engineers. Peng
14   Decl. (Dkt. 335-31) ¶¶ 90-94. The August 1, 2025 “OTalk” was an introductory, company-wide talk on
15   OPPO’s internal speaker-series platform addressing high-level, generally known sensor-development
16   concepts. Peng Decl. (Dkt. 335-31) ¶¶ 103–109. Apple’s “hundreds of engineers” characterization is
17   further misleading: the OTalk was a general audience talk open to all employees, not a presentation to just
18   engineers, and a person attending would not have understood it to disclose any company’s proprietary
19   information. Id. OPPO neither solicited, encouraged, nor approved the misappropriation of any third
20   party’s information, and it disputes Apple’s characterization of the communications Apple attributes to
21   Dr. Shi and Dr. Zeng, including the isolated phrases Apple quotes about collecting and sharing
22   information. Those communications are presented out of context, and do not bear the meaning Apple
23   assigns them. Zeng Decl. (Dkt. 193) ¶¶ 5-8.
24          For these reasons, the Court should deny Apple’s motion for a preliminary injunction. Apple has
25   not shown a likelihood of success on the merits, because the information at issue is publicly known or
26   readily ascertainable and there is no evidence that OPPO ever received, used, or disclosed any Apple trade
27   secret. Nor can Apple show imminent, irreparable harm, given that any information Dr. Shi is alleged to
28   have disclosed has been quarantined and was never used in OPPO’s business, and that Apple’s PPG-

 1   related information became public upon the commercial release of its AirPods with PPG sensors in
 2   September 2025. The balance of hardships and the public interest likewise weigh against an injunction
 3   that would chill OPPO's use of its own independently developed technology.
 4          Separately, Dr. Zeng should be permitted to return to work immediately. The investigation that
 5   justified the interim measures has concluded and confirmed that Dr. Zeng has no unique knowledge of or
 6   access to any alleged Apple trade secret, and he was, at most, exposed to the same handful of slides shown
 7   to many other OPPO employees. There is no factual or legal basis to single Dr. Zeng out for restrictions
 8   more onerous than those applicable to OPPO generally, and California law and policy disfavor restraints
 9   that keep an employee from practicing his profession. See Dkt. 382 at pp. 12-13. The interim measures as
10   to Dr. Zeng should therefore be lifted.
11                   2.     Innopeak’s Statement
12          InnoPeak is an American company headquartered in Palo Alto, California. While it shares a
13   corporate parent with OPPO, InnoPeak is a separate company. It does not manufacture, market, or sell
14   commercial products, but rather focuses exclusively on research and development. Tan Decl. (Dkt. No.
15   228) ¶¶ 3–4, 7. Apple’s sole claim against InnoPeak—for purported violation of the DTSA—is meritless.
16          InnoPeak hired Dr. Shi to fill a research-and-development role. During the hiring process,
17   InnoPeak identified Dr. Shi as a candidate based on his generalized experience and knowledge. Yin Decl.
18   (Dkt. No. 333-39) ¶¶ 4, 9. And Dr. Shi did not provide any Apple confidential information to InnoPeak
19   during his hiring process. Rather, he was repeatedly instructed not to use or disclose any Apple
20   confidential information. Further, as a condition of employment, InnoPeak required him to execute a
21   confidentiality agreement confirming that he had not taken any confidential information from Apple. See
22   id. ¶¶ 15–16.
23          Immediately after Apple informed InnoPeak of its intention to sue, InnoPeak placed Dr. Shi on
24   administrative leave and conducted its own review of Dr. Shi’s actions. InnoPeak reviewed Dr. Shi’s
25   forensic activity and exhaustively searched communications and other materials related to Dr. Shi’s work
26   during the seven weeks that he was active at InnoPeak. Connolly Decl. (Dkt. No. 333-43) ¶¶ 54-65. In
27   addition, InnoPeak responded to Apple’s broad-reaching discovery requests, and had numerous witnesses

 1   testify under oath about its research projects and operations. Apple did not once seek the Court’s
 2   intervention to broaden the scope of InnoPeak’s investigation.
 3          InnoPeak found no evidence that Dr. Shi disclosed any Apple trade secrets or that InnoPeak itself
 4   used, disclosed, or misappropriated any trade secrets. Indeed, no Apple documents were found on
 5   InnoPeak’s systems—including any of the files that Apple claims Dr. Shi exfiltrated. See id. ¶ 8. And not
 6   only did Dr. Shi’s presentations merely reiterate publicly known or readily ascertainable information, but
 7   also InnoPeak had no use for much of the information that Apple purportedly asserts as a trade secret.
 8   Indeed, Apple was able to point to only one InnoPeak-specific project where Dr. Shi allegedly disclosed
 9   confidential Apple product information. See, e.g., Mar. 10, 2026 Hr’g Tr. 68:10–13. But even that project
10   reflected information about PPG earbuds that was known before Dr. Shi joined InnoPeak and was even
11   later disclosed by Apple. See Efimov Suppl. Decl. (Dkt. No. 336-36) ¶ 15.
12                  3.     Dr. Zeng’s Statement
13          Dr. Zijing Zeng is an experienced executive and engineer who has dedicated his career to the
14   healthcare, technology, and research & development spaces. Dr. Zeng has worked for over 18 years in
15   health sensor research and development, and his inventions have earned him over 40 personal patents. At
16   OPPO, Dr. Zeng was an Associate Vice President and Head of OPPO Health where he built the OPPO
17   Health Lab from scratch into an organization with more than 120 engineers that helped generate more
18   than 100 patents and 10 papers. Dr. Zeng and his team have developed health technologies that help
19   millions of users improve their health.
20          Dr. Zeng’s interactions with Dr. Shi arose in the ordinary course of recruiting for a legitimate
21   business need. In April 2025, Dr. Zeng had been looking for over a year to fill a role on the sensor team
22   following the departure of a critical employee. Apple’s allegations distort Dr. Zeng’s routine recruitment
23   communications and salary discussions with Dr. Shi. Dr. Zeng did not request, suggest, or have any
24   awareness that Dr. Shi—as alleged by Apple—took confidential materials in the lead-up to his departure
25   from Apple.     Dr. Zeng would never condone misappropriation of any third party’s confidential
26   information. Consistent with that principle, following Dr. Shi’s hire by InnoPeak, Dr. Zeng never
27   prompted Dr. Shi to provide or present on any confidential Apple information.
28

 1          Following the initiation of this litigation, Dr. Zeng was placed on administrative leave from OPPO
 2   without any ability to access OPPO’s or InnoPeak’s “systems or facilities.” See Dkt. No. 30 (the “Interim
 3   Measures.”) His 20-year career was, in effect, frozen. It has now been nearly a year since the Interim
 4   Measures were put into place. Every day Dr. Zeng remains excluded from the OPPO Health Lab—the
 5   organization he built from the ground up—causes serious and escalating harm. As discussed at the hearing
 6   on Apple’s Motion for a Preliminary Injunction, the ongoing restrictions of the Interim Measures have
 7   jeopardized Dr. Zeng’s position at OPPO, and the longer he remains sidelined, the less likely it will be
 8   that he will have a position to return to.
 9                  4.      Dr. Shi’s Statement
10          Dr. Chen Shi is an engineer with substantial experience in health sensing technologies. Apple
11   employed Dr. Shi from January 2020 until June 2025, after which he accepted employment with
12   InnoPeak.1 Apple subsequently filed this action asserting a single claim against Dr. Shi for alleged breach
13   of his Intellectual Property Agreement ("IPA"), while asserting trade secret misappropriation claims
14   against the corporate defendants and Dr. Zeng.
15          Dr. Shi denies that he is liable to Apple and disputes Apple's characterization of the facts and
16   applicable law. He further disputes that Apple is entitled to the injunctive or monetary relief it seeks
17   against him.
18          Since the commencement of this action, Dr. Shi has complied with the Court's orders, including
19   the Interim Measures entered shortly after the filing of the Complaint. He participated in expedited
20   discovery, including the forensic collection of his electronic devices and accounts, the production of
21   documents, written discovery, and deposition discovery. Dr. Shi will continue to comply with his
22   obligations under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and this Court's orders as discovery proceeds.
23          Dr. Shi intends to vigorously defend against Apple's claims and reserves all rights, defenses,
24   privileges, and objections available under applicable law.

 1   III.    LEGAL ISSUES
 2           This case for misappropriation under the Defend Trade Secrets Act and breach of contract has and
 3   will involve at least the following legal issues. The Parties reserve the right to amend this identification
 4   of issues as the litigation progresses:
 5              Whether Apple has properly identified any cognizable trade secrets;
 6              Whether Apple’s asserted trade secrets derive independent economic value, actual or potential,
 7               from not being generally known to, and not being readily ascertainable through proper means
 8               by, another person who can obtain economic value from the disclosure or use of that
 9               information; and whether Apple has taken reasonable measures to protect those trade secrets
10               from disclosure;
11              Whether Defendants OPPO, InnoPeak, and/or Dr. Zeng have each misappropriated Apple’s
12               asserted trade secrets as defined in 18 U.S.C. § 1839(5), and whether the misappropriation has
13               been willful and malicious;
14              Whether Apple can establish that Dr. Shi has breached his Intellectual Property Agreement
15               (IPA);
16              Whether the IPA is enforceable to the extent Apple seeks relief inconsistent with applicable
17               California law, including California Business and Professions Code section 16600;
18              Whether Apple can establish that any alleged breach of the IPA by Dr. Shi caused it
19               recoverable damages;
20              Whether Apple is entitled to damages for misappropriation under the DTSA pursuant to 18
21               U.S.C. § 1836(b)(3)(B) and breach of contract;
22              The amount of damages, prejudgment interest, and post-judgment interest recoverable by
23               Apple, if any, if Defendants OPPO, InnoPeak, and/or Dr. Zeng are found to have
24               misappropriated Apple’s trade secrets and/or if Dr. Shi is found to have breached his IPA;
25              Whether Apple is entitled to exemplary damages pursuant to 18 U.S.C. § 1836(b)(3)(C);
26              Whether Apple or any Defendant is entitled to attorneys’ fees pursuant to 18 U.S.C. §
27               1836(b)(3)(D);
